If a joint extraction in $A_j$ units has comparison $\lambda D$, then every fixed offset $t\in\mathbb Z$ has $$k_-\lambda4^{pt} \leq \liminf\frac{A_{j+t}}{A_j} \leq \limsup\frac{A_{j+t}}{A_j} \leq k_+\lambda4^{pt}. \label{met:rigid-ratios}$$ In particular $\lambda\in[k_+^{-1},k_-^{-1}]$. The statement includes forward offsets whose ratios were first extracted in $[0,\infty]$.
  - Explanation: Bounds fixed-offset normalizer ratios in a rigid law and controls its scalar uniformly over extracted laws.
- **claim-comparable-preceding-power-ratios** (bound, [source](#stmt-met-majority)): Suppose a joint extraction at scales $j\to\infty$ satisfies the following tests at every fixed preceding offset: adjacent $A$-ratios lie in a fixed compact subinterval of $(0,\infty)$, there is the normalized upper circuit quantile, and a fixed sufficiently high-probability normalized lower traversal test holds. Then $$r_i:=4^{pi}\lim\frac{A_{j-i}}{A_j},\qquad i\geq0,$$ can be extracted with $r_i\in(0,\infty)$, and one constant $L_0$ satisfies $L_0^{-2}\leq r_i\leq L_0^2$ for all $i$.
  - Explanation: Uses overlapping majority bands to bound every preceding power-rescaled ratio by common positive constants.
- **claim-all-scale-port-normalization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-met-normalizers)): There is a deterministic positive function $B(n)$, tending to infinity, and constants $s>0$, $K<\infty$ such that $$\frac{B(n')}{B(n)}\leq K\left(\frac{n'}n\right)^s, \qquad 1\leq n'\leq n. \label{met:polynomial-ratio}$$ One can take $s=p/2$ and $B(n)=A_{\lfloor\log_4n\rfloor}$, after changing finitely many initial values.* *Along every deterministic sequence of diverging time units, joint crossing-data extractions in $B(n)$ units have local comparison $\lambda D$ with a deterministic $\lambda$ in a fixed compact subinterval of $(0,\infty)$, after further extraction. The comparison includes all finite-cost lower certificates, complete ordered-port upper following, the simultaneous small surrounding circuits of Lemma <a href="#met:vanishing-joins" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="met:vanishing-joins">76</a>, and finite connected systems of paths with prescribed transverse intersections. The same comparison holds on every ordinary compact patch of a conditioned finite-sphere extraction using these deterministic units and the common local kernels.
  - Explanation: Propagates deterministic normalizers across all diverging time units and transfers rigid local comparisons to finite-sphere patches.
- **claim-complete-spatial-distance-graph** (theorem, [source](#stmt-comp-metric-graph)): In every joint subsequential extraction supplied by Theorems <a href="#conf:canonical" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="conf:canonical">55</a> and <a href="#met:normalizers" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="met:normalizers">90</a>, one may further extract the intrinsic spaces $(V_n,\delta_n)$ and their spatial distance graphs. Almost surely, every resulting limit of the latter is $$\label{comp:target-graph} \mathcal G_D =\{(z,w,D(z,w)):z,w\in\widehat{\mathbb C}\}.$$ Consequently $$(\mu_n,K_n(a_n))\ \Longrightarrow\ (\mu^+,\mathcal G_{D^+})$$ through all positive integers. In any convergent joint extraction with additional reference or local observations, its metric component is the same graph <a href="#comp:target-graph" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="comp:target-graph">[comp:target-graph]</a>. The Hausdorff metric for the second component is that induced by $\rho(z,z')+\rho(w,w')+\|r-r'\|$.
  - Explanation: Identifies the full spatial distance graph in every joint extraction and obtains full-sequence canonical metric and area convergence.
- **claim-all-vertex-location-relation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-comp-relation)): Suppose that, on a coupled subsequence, $(V_n,\delta_n)$ converges in Gromov–Hausdorff distance to a compact metric space $(Y,d_Y)$, and that $z_n(V_n)$ becomes dense in $\widehat{\mathbb C}$. There are maps $j_n:V_n\to Y$ and numbers $e_n\downarrow0$ such that $$\label{comp:approximation} \left\|d_Y(j_n(u),j_n(v))-\delta_n(u,v)\right\|\le e_n, \qquad \sup_{y\in Y}\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_{d_Y}(y,j_n(V_n))\le e_n.$$ After a further subsequence, the finite sets $$R_n=\{(j_n(v),z_n(v)):v\in V_n\}$$ converge in Hausdorff distance in $Y\times\widehat{\mathbb C}$ to a compact relation $R$ that projects onto both factors. On the same subsequence, $$\label{comp:relation-graph} K_n(a_n)\longrightarrow \mathcal K(R):= \{(z,w,d_Y(y,y')):(y,z),(y',w)\in R\}.$$
  - Explanation: Retains every vertex through a compact location relation and expresses the limiting distance graph directly from that relation.
- **claim-collapsing-separator-avoidance** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-comp-avoid-separator)): Assume <a href="#comp:approximation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="comp:approximation">[comp:approximation]</a>. Let $y_0\in Y$, and suppose that $Y\setminus\{y_0\}$ is path connected. If $$\sup_{v\in S_n}d_Y(j_n(v),y_0)\longrightarrow0,$$ then, for any vertices $u_n,v_n$ with $j_n(u_n)\to y$ and $j_n(v_n)\to y'$ in $Y\setminus\{y_0\}$, the two vertices are in the same component of $G_n\setminus S_n$ for all sufficiently large $n$. The conclusion also holds when $y=y'$.
  - Explanation: Uses path connectivity of a punctured intrinsic limit to join vertices while avoiding a collapsing discrete separator.
- **claim-area-mark-small-bypasses** (theorem, [source](#stmt-comp-root-bypass)): Almost surely there are rectifiable closed paths $L_k$ in $\widehat{\mathbb C}\setminus\{p_*\}$, each separating $p_*$ from the complement of a neighborhood of $p_*$, whose spatial diameters and $D$-lengths tend to zero. Consequently, for $z,w\ne p_*$, the internal distance in $\widehat{\mathbb C}\setminus\{p_*\}$ equals $D(z,w)$. The metric completion of that punctured space is $(\widehat{\mathbb C},D)$.
  - Explanation: Provides arbitrarily small rectifiable bypasses around the exploration root and identifies the punctured metric completion.
- **claim-bounded-comparison-scales** (bound, [source](#stmt-comp-scales)): The sequence $a_nB(n)$ is bounded. On every deterministic subsequence one may therefore pass to a further deterministic subsequence on which $$\label{comp:alpha} a_nB(n)\longrightarrow\alpha\in[0,\infty).$$ In a joint extraction on this subsequence, let $\lambda$ be the deterministic positive multiplier of Theorem <a href="#met:normalizers" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="met:normalizers">90</a>. In $\delta_n$-units, local port following has upper factor $\alpha\lambda$. If $\alpha>0$, the lower certificate comparison has that same factor.* *Almost surely, about every spatial point there are shrinking strict primal separating circuits whose limiting $\delta_n$-diameters tend to zero. Moreover, if $\alpha=0$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are connected primal skeletons of $\delta_n$-diameter tending to zero whose complementary spatial components have diameter at most $\varepsilon$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
  - Explanation: Bounds intrinsic times passage normalizers and produces vanishing intrinsic separators, including fine connected skeletons in the zero-scale case.
- **claim-positive-scale-singleton-fibers** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-comp-positive-fibers)): If $\alpha>0$, then $R$ is the graph of a homeomorphism $\pi:Y\to\widehat{\mathbb C}$, and $$\label{comp:proportionality} d_Y(y,y')=\alpha\lambda D(\pi(y),\pi(y')) \qquad(y,y'\in Y).$$ In particular, $$\label{comp:endpoint-modulus} \lim_{r\downarrow0}\limsup_{n\to\infty} \sup_{\substack{u,v\in V_n\\\rho(z_n(u),z_n(v))\le r}} \delta_n(u,v)=0.$$
  - Explanation: Identifies the location relation as a homeomorphism and obtains uniform all-vertex endpoint continuity at positive scale.
- **claim-zero-scale-cross-relation** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-comp-concentration)): If $\alpha=0$, there are unique points $y_0\in Y$ and $z_0\in\widehat{\mathbb C}$ such that $$\label{comp:cross-relation} R=(\{y_0\}\times\widehat{\mathbb C})\ \cup\ (Y\times\{z_0\}).$$ Moreover $z_0$ is a measurable function of the limiting distance graph $\mathcal K(R)$ alone. It is the unique point $z$ for which $$\label{comp:positive-diagonal} (z,z,r)\in\mathcal K(R)\quad\hbox{for some }r>0.$$
  - Explanation: Characterizes the hypothetical zero-scale relation as a cross and recovers its unique spatial center from positive diagonal graph heights.
- **claim-concentration-root-avoidance** (theorem, [source](#stmt-comp-root-avoidance)): In the setting of Proposition <a href="#comp:concentration" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="comp:concentration">97</a>, almost surely $z_0\ne p_*$.
  - Explanation: Uses diffuse conditional root sampling to keep the hypothetical concentration center away from the exploration root.
- **claim-no-zero-scale-concentration** (theorem, [source](#stmt-comp-no-concentration)): The alternative $\alpha=0$ is impossible.
  - Explanation: Excludes the zero passage-scale alternative by placing separated positive escape tests in one actual sphere law.
- **claim-common-reflection-law** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-joint-reflection)): Let $E$ be a measurable space with a measurable involution $\mathfrak r$. Suppose random elements $X,Y$ satisfy $X\in\{Y,\mathfrak rY\}$ almost surely, and both $\mathop{\mathrm{Law}}(X)$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{Law}}(Y)$ are invariant under $\mathfrak r$. Then $\mathop{\mathrm{Law}}(X)=\mathop{\mathrm{Law}}(Y)$. The choice between $Y$ and $\mathfrak rY$ may depend on the entire coupled random object.
  - Explanation: Removes an adaptively chosen common reflection when both marginal laws are reflection invariant.
- **claim-positive-scalar-law-rigidity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-comp-scalar)): If $X$ is a finite, strictly positive random variable and $c>0$ is deterministic, then $cX$ and $X$ have the same law only if $c=1$.
  - Explanation: Forces a deterministic scale preserving a finite strictly positive random observable's law to be trivial.

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-enc-contour-limits",
        "exact_quote": "Let $$\\varrho=\\frac b{1-b}=-\\cos\\left(\\frac{\\pi\\gamma^2}{4}\\right),\n \\qquad \\gamma\\in(\\sqrt2,2),\\qquad \\kappa=\\frac{16}{\\gamma^2}.$$ The diffusively rescaled bilateral resolved contours converge, uniformly on compact time intervals in law, to a bilateral Brownian motion whose marginal variance rates are one and whose correlation is $\\varrho$. For a length-$2n$ word conditioned to reduce to the empty word, the same rescaling, with duration one, converges uniformly in law to the corresponding quadrant Brownian excursion from $(0,0)$ to $(0,0)$.*\n\n*For an unconditioned raw block of $O(n)$ letters, the number of flexible orders left unidentified by reduction of the block is $o_{\\mathbb P}(\\sqrt n)$.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-enc-peanosphere",
        "exact_quote": "The bilateral Brownian contour is the boundary-length process of a $\\gamma$-quantum cone explored by an independent, unparameterized whole-plane space-filling $\\mathrm{SLE}_{\\kappa}$, subsequently parameterized by quantum area. The duration-one excursion is the boundary-length process of the ordinary unit-area $\\gamma$-quantum sphere explored in the same way from an area-typical marked point $p_*$. The contour determines the curve-decorated quantum surface up to its marked conformal equivalence.*\n\n*Write $\\eta$ for the exploration parameterized by quantum area. In either realization, $\\eta_*(\\mathrm dt)=\\mu_h$. Its spatial identifications are generated by finite chains of scalar horizontal chords $$\\label{enc:chord-rule}\n s\\sim_L t\\quad\\Longleftrightarrow\\quad\n L_s=L_t=\\inf_{[s,t]}L,\n \\qquad s<t,$$ and the analogous $R$-chords, with the usual endpoint identification for the sphere. The resulting quotient carries the topology of the plane, or sphere, respectively. Frontier arcs are parameterized by quantum length, with running-minimum contour heights as their length coordinates.",

      },

        "anchor": "stmt-enc-sphere-representation",
        "exact_quote": "Let $h_{\\mathbb C}$ be the whole-plane Gaussian free field (GFF) with circle average zero on $\\partial\\mathbb D$, and put $$|z|_+=\\max\\{1,|z|\\},\\qquad\n G_{\\mathbb C}(z,w)=\\log\\frac{|z|_+|w|_+}{|z-w|},\\qquad\n Q=\\frac2\\gamma+\\frac\\gamma2.$$ Define $$\\label{enc:liouville-field}\n h_L=h_{\\mathbb C}+\\gamma G_{\\mathbb C}(0,\\cdot)+\\gamma G_{\\mathbb C}(1,\\cdot)\n       -(2Q-\\gamma)\\log|\\cdot|_+,\n \\quad A=\\mu_{h_L}(\\mathbb C).$$ Tilt the law of $h_L$ by the integrable strictly positive density $A^{4/\\gamma^2-2}/\\mathbb E[A^{4/\\gamma^2-2}]$, and then set $$\\label{enc:area-normalization}\n h=h_L-\\gamma^{-1}\\log A.$$ The result is the ordinary unit-area sphere with three independent area marks embedded at $\\infty,0,1$. Resampling its three area marks and renormalizing gives the same law. In particular, on any bounded region avoiding $0,1$, its field modulo constants is locally mutually absolutely continuous with a whole-plane GFF modulo constants. Near $0$, away from $1$, the corresponding comparison field is $h_{\\mathbb C}-\\gamma\\log|\\cdot|$.",
        "source_id": "PM-211.4"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {

        "anchor": "stmt-top-scalar-trees",
        "exact_quote": "If $c_n\\to c$ uniformly, then $$\\sup_{s,t}|d_{c_n}(s,t)-d_c(s,t)|\n \\le 4\\|c_n-c\\|_\\infty.$$ Suppose $s_n\\to s$, $t_n\\to t$, and $d_c(s,t)=0$. Every contour representative of every vertex on the discrete $c_n$-tree path between the vertices at $s_n,t_n$ has distance $d_{c_n}$ tending to zero from the vertex at $s_n$, uniformly over those representatives. Consequently, if $c$ is $L$ or $R$, their images under $\\eta$ tend uniformly to $\\eta(s)$.*\n\n*For $c_n=R_n$, take the faces represented by the vertices of this dual-tree path.         "anchor": "stmt-top-protected-window",
        "exact_quote": "Work in a bilateral contour coupling with locally uniform convergence to its peanosphere contour. The inverse images of the tested compact sets are contained in the unchanged part.         "anchor": "stmt-enc-cone-estimates",
        "exact_quote": "Set $$\\theta=\\arccos(-\\varrho)=\\frac{\\pi\\gamma^2}{4},\\qquad\n d_0=0,\\quad d_1=\\frac12,\\quad d_2=\\frac{\\pi}{2\\theta}\n       =\\frac2{\\gamma^2}>\\frac12.$$ For fixed positive duration, the probability that Brownian motion stays above $-\\varepsilon$ in $k$ specified coordinates is at most $C\\varepsilon^{2d_k}$, for $k=1,2$.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-enc-chord-genericity",
        "exact_quote": "Almost surely the bilateral contour, and the interior of the quadrant excursion, have the following properties simultaneously.*\n\n1.  *There is no positive-span common $L$- and $R$-chord.*\n\n2.  *At a forward or backward joint record with positive witness, neither coordinate is at a scalar branch level anywhere in the time domain.*\n\n3.  *If both backward supplier chords at a time have positive span, each supplier is unique, their times are distinct, and neither scalar chord class is a branch triple. More precisely, fix a compact time window $J$ and $a>0$. The admissible tuples $(t,s_L,s_R)\\in J^3$ with $t-s_L,t-s_R\\ge a$ form a compact set, and $|s_L-s_R|$ is bounded below on it whenever it is nonempty. For uniformly converging contour perturbations, admissible supplier tuples in $J^3$ with these span bounds converge along subsequences to such tuples. Their more-recent-supplier choice is therefore stable in a neighborhood of each limiting tuple, uniformly on this compact set.",

        "anchor": "stmt-ker-frontier-overlap",
        "exact_quote": "Almost surely the following holds simultaneously for the countable block atlas. A positive aligned overlap of two frontiers of the same scalar colour identifies the corresponding points in that scalar tree. Its parameter translation is the difference of their actual used-start heights.         "exact_quote": "Let $c$ be one of the two limiting contours on a compact interval $J$. Let $I\\subset J$ be open and contain $\\eta^{-1}(K)\\cap J$ for a compact set $K$, and let $O=J\\setminus I$. Consider a compact family $\\mathcal C$ of triples $(s,t,h)$, $s\\le t$, such that $$c(s)=c(t)=h,\\qquad \\eta(s)\\in K,\\qquad\n c(u)\\ge h\\quad (u\\in[s,t]\\cap I).$$ There is $\\delta>0$ such that, whenever $[s,t]\\cap O\\ne\\varnothing$ and $(s,t,h)\\in\\mathcal C$, $$\\label{top:minimum-gap}\n \\left|\\min_{[s,t]\\cap O}c-h\\right|>\\delta.$$ Consequently the omitted pieces cannot change an exact gluing decision at heights tending to a protected candidate height without either a retained obstruction or a strict height gap.",

        "anchor": "stmt-ker-incidences",
        "exact_quote": "Fix $K\\Subset U$, finitely many local tests, and a contour realization on the common probability-one event of Lemmas <a href=\"#enc:chord-genericity\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"enc:chord-genericity\">25</a> and <a href=\"#ker:frontier-overlap\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ker:frontier-overlap\">27</a>. There exists a chart instruction retaining every time preimage and full star needed by the tests. It has a continuum input neighborhood on which the omitted-obstruction and supplier-order tests have fixed strict margins. For all sufficiently large discrete indices, its realization gives the exact required incidences by recomputing retained equalities and minima from the raw words and forest offsets.         "exact_quote": "Fix a countable atlas of protected charts and countably many observations from Lemma <a href=\"#ker:readouts\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ker:readouts\">31</a>. From every sequence of integer scales tending to infinity and arbitrary deterministic cost units one can extract jointly kernels $K(I,\\mathrm dO)$ with the following properties.*\n\n1.  *In the bilateral word and in the interior of the finite empty-word bridge, the conditional output law given $\\mathcal C$ is $K(I,\\mathrm dO)$. The finite-bridge assertion refers to the actual joint finite-sphere observations on the chosen subsequence.*\n\n2.  *For disjoint closed real buffers, the conditional joint law given $\\mathcal C$ is the product of their kernels. Each buffer may carry a whole countable array of observations and refinements. Overlapping descriptions of one observation agree through their common union chart.*\n\n3.  *Smooth positive changes of the reference input densities do not change these kernels on their common input law. Consequently a locally absolutely continuous change of continuum field law uses the same kernels; a dominated field law gives dominated joint laws.*\n\n4.  *The extraction may retain all fixed deterministic ratios of microscopic time scales in a countable list, together with their actual joint input laws. The output cost units may be arbitrary deterministic positive numbers.*\n\n*Fixed measurable continuum functionals, including the reference internal metrics of the LQG surface, may be included jointly.         "anchor": "stmt-ker-finite-order",
        "exact_quote": "For a compact protection $K$ in a bounded open real buffer $V$, only finitely many traversals of $V$ meet $K$, almost surely. After retaining their local directed pieces, their remaining global order is a finite permutation. Conditional on the local imaginary input $J$, write $$w_o(J)=\\mathbb P[\\text{order}=o\\mid J].$$ Its feasible values are those with $w_o(J)>0$; the actual order is feasible almost surely. These weights depend neither on the real field nor on the choice of quantum time unit.*\n\n*For every finite protected test, the necessary order is determined by the imaginary field in a sufficiently large finite buffer, on events whose probabilities tend to one as that buffer increases. The number of traversals can also be bounded deterministically on an exhaustion of probability tending to one.*\n\n*The kernels can be augmented to include an output for every feasible order, simultaneously for all retained fixed scale offsets. Given the entire real and imaginary fields, the law of this augmented vector depends only on their respective local restrictions; such vectors have product laws in disjoint buffered regions. One component is the actual output at the actual order.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-ker-field-transfer",
        "exact_quote": "On strict buffered compact subsets away from marked singularities, ordinary GFF restrictions, cone restrictions in an appropriate fixed chart, and their finite smooth shifts are locally mutually absolutely continuous. Restrictions on finitely many separated buffers are jointly equivalent to independent ordinary restrictions. The same statements hold for the independent imaginary field modulo its angular period, using its uniform phase. These changes transfer the kernels of Theorem <a href=\"#ker:local-kernels\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ker:local-kernels\">32</a>, their products, and the all-order vectors of Lemma <a href=\"#ker:finite-order\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ker:finite-order\">37</a>.*\n\n*The kernels are intrinsically covariant under affine coordinate changes. For $\\psi(z)=az+b$, $a\\ne0$, transform simultaneously $$h\\longmapsto h\\circ\\psi+Q\\log|a|,\\qquad\n \\widetilde h\\longmapsto\\widetilde h\\circ\\psi-\\chi\\arg a,\n \\quad \\chi=2/\\gamma-\\gamma/2.$$ Transform ports and ranges by $\\psi^{-1}$. Quantum durations, frontier lengths, raw graph costs, and flag-surface extremal lengths are unchanged. In particular translations preserve every chosen deterministic cost unit.*\n\n\n*There is also an exact indexed change of quantum units. If the original time unit is $n$ and the cost denominator is $c_n$, express the same map using time unit $vn$ and cost denominator $c_nv^p$. Its field input, time labels, frontier lengths, and costs become, respectively, $$\\label{ker:units}\n h_v=h-\\gamma^{-1}\\log v,\\qquad\n t_v=v^{-1}t,\\qquad \\ell_v=v^{-1/2}\\ell,\n \\qquad O_v=v^{-p}O.$$ These identities hold jointly for the indexed kernel arrays. They also hold with $h+b$ in place of $h$. They assert a re-expression of the same array, not equality of two differently indexed kernels. For any other deterministic output denominator $d_{n,v}>0$, the last factor is instead its literal ratio $c_n/d_{n,v}$; in particular extremal length divided by the same denominator in both conventions has no additional power of $v$.",
        "source_id": "PM-211.4"
      },
      "evidence": [

Restrictions on finitely many separated buffers are jointly equivalent to independent ordinary restrictions. The same statements hold for the independent imaginary field modulo its angular period, using its uniform phase. These changes transfer the kernels of Theorem <a href=\"#ker:local-kernels\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ker:local-kernels\">32</a>, their products, and the all-order vectors of Lemma <a href=\"#ker:finite-order\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ker:finite-order\">37</a>.*\n\n*The kernels are intrinsically covariant under affine coordinate changes. For $\\psi(z)=az+b$, $a\\ne0$, transform simultaneously $$h\\longmapsto h\\circ\\psi+Q\\log|a|,\\qquad\n \\widetilde h\\longmapsto\\widetilde h\\circ\\psi-\\chi\\arg a,\n \\quad \\chi=2/\\gamma-\\gamma/2.$$ Transform ports and ranges by $\\psi^{-1}$. Quantum durations, frontier lengths, raw graph costs, and flag-surface extremal lengths are unchanged. In particular translations preserve every chosen deterministic cost unit.*\n\n\n*There is also an exact indexed change of quantum units. If the original time unit is $n$ and the cost denominator is $c_n$, express the same map using time unit $vn$ and cost denominator $c_nv^p$. Its field input, time labels, frontier lengths, and costs become, respectively, $$\\label{ker:units}\n h_v=h-\\gamma^{-1}\\log v,\\qquad\n t_v=v^{-1}t,\\qquad \\ell_v=v^{-1/2}\\ell,\n \\qquad O_v=v^{-p}O.$$ These identities hold jointly for the indexed kernel arrays. They also hold with $h+b$ in place of $h$. They assert a re-expression of the same array, not equality of two differently indexed kernels. For any other deterministic output denominator $d_{n,v}>0$, the last factor is instead its literal ratio $c_n/d_{n,v}$; in particular extremal length divided by the same denominator in both conventions has no additional power of $v$.",
      "explanation": "Transfers kernels through local field equivalence and records exact affine covariance and indexed quantum-unit changes.",

        "exact_quote": "Let the real input have one fixed ordinary pinned Gaussian law, and let $f_j$ be a finite list of deterministic smooth functions in its Cameron–Martin space. The pin and its law are chosen before the auxiliary draws or any event selection. For recipe $j$, suppose $f_j=b_j$ on a preservation buffer $V_j$ and $f_j=0$ outside a larger support buffer $W_j$. Before selecting a recipe, sample an auxiliary local output from the kernel with input $h+b_j$ in $V_j$, independently of the original outputs outside $W_j$, conditional on the fields.           "exact_quote": "There are constants $C,\\Lambda$, depending only on the fixed shell geometry and $s$, such that the centered Gaussian vector $$Z=\\bigl((H_j-H_{j-1})_{1\\le j\\le m},\n              (G_j,\\widetilde G_j)_{0\\le j\\le m}\\bigr)\n \\quad\\hbox{in}\\quad\n \\mathbb R^m\\oplus\\bigoplus_{j=0}^m L^2(E^+)^2$$ has covariance operator norm at most $\\Lambda$ and trace at most $C(m+1)$, once the largest radius is sufficiently small.",

        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-ann-gaussian-budget",
          "exact_quote": "Consequently, when $m\\le C_0N$, for each $R<\\infty$ one can choose $A<\\infty$ so that $$\\mathbb P\\left[\n  \\sum_{j=1}^m(H_j-H_{j-1})^2+\n  \\sum_{j=0}^m\\bigl(\\|G_j\\|_2^2+\\|\\widetilde G_j\\|_2^2\\bigr)\n       >AN\\right]\\le e^{-RN}.\n \\label{ann:square-tail}$$",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-ann-aligned-annuli",
        "exact_quote": "Fix $\\theta>0$ and $M>0$. For each integer $N$ in any unbounded deterministic set, let $$I_N\\subset[N,2N]\\cap\\mathbb Z,\\qquad |I_N|\\ge\\theta N,\\qquad\n v_i=M4^{-i}.$$ Consider local unit events $\\mathcal G_{N,i}$, $i\\in I_N$, for the arrays of Theorem <a href=\"#ker:local-kernels\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"ker:local-kernels\">32</a>, on the fixed shell $E$. Their reference probabilities are evaluated under the single normalized ordinary field law specified above, at every label. The events may vary with $N,i$; the local field law and full buffer geometry do not. There are constants $$0<a<B<\\infty,\\quad c>0,\\quad \\varepsilon_*>0$$ depending only on $\\gamma,\\theta$ and the fixed buffer geometries, with the following implication. If every $\\mathcal G_{N,i}$ has reference probability at least $1-\\varepsilon_*$, then in an ordinary field chart every compact set $K$ has, almost surely for all sufficiently large admissible $N$, a collection of good transplanted tests such that:*\n\n1.  *There are at most $CN$ radii, all in $[e^{-BN},e^{-aN}]$. At each radius the centers belong to a deterministic square grid of spacing $\\epsilon_0r$. At each fixed radius the buffers have overlap bounded by a fixed constant.*\n\n2.  *Every $x\\in K$ has at least $cN$ good tests at distinct radii $r$, with centers $c_r$ satisfying $|x-c_r|<r/256$. In particular $x$ lies with strict clearance in each central hole $B(c_r,r/128)$.*\n\n3.  *Each test has a label in $I_N$, is evaluated by <a href=\"#ann:normalized-field\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"ann:normalized-field\">[ann:normalized-field]</a>, and succeeds for the actual traversal order. At most a fixed number of labels are used at any one center and radius; one may retain a single successful test there.*\n\n*Under the ordinary Gaussian law, failure probabilities are bounded by $C_Ke^{-c_KN}$ and hence are summable. The almost sure eventual conclusion persists under any fixed locally absolutely continuous change of the joint field law, with the same local kernels. It holds simultaneously over countably many compact sets and test families satisfying the stated hypotheses.",

        "anchor": "stmt-met-chain",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose every point of a compact set $K$ belongs to a central hole of a finite family of buffered annuli contained in an open set $U$. Their largest outer radius is at most $r_*$, their holes have a fixed positive clearance from their bands, and their reference weights are $w_i>0$. Assume that a reference path from a hole to its surrounding separator has $D$-length at least $a w_i$, where $a>0$.*\n\n1.  *If the $i$th annulus contains an attainable surrounding primal circuit of cost at most $Lw_i$, then every $D$-rectifiable path in $K$ can be followed, with endpoint errors tending to zero with $r_*$, at cost at most $$\\frac{L}{a}\\operatorname{len}_D(P)+L\\max_i w_i.$$ For any fixed finite ordered subdivision of the reference path, the following walk can also retain its intermediate ports. Each marked subpassage has cost at most $(L/a)$ times the corresponding reference length plus $2L\\max_iw_i$. All spatial errors are $O(r_*)$, and arbitrary fixed open tube losses are allowed.*\n\n2.  *Suppose instead that every primal traversal from the hole side to the outside of the band costs at least $\\ell w_i$. Suppose also that a fixed reference circle lies strictly outside the tested band and strictly inside its buffer, with internal $D$-diameter at most $Aw_i$ in that buffer. Every bounded-cost certificate from $x$ to $y$ whose range lies in $K$ then satisfies $$\\operatorname{cost}\\geq \\frac{\\ell}{A}D(x,y)-o_{r_*}(1).$$ The error depends only on the reference metric modulus on the fixed compact neighborhood of $K$.*\n\n*Both conclusions hold for limits of discrete paths when the annular tests have strict margins and all selected ordered subrecords are retained.",

        "anchor": "stmt-met-vanishing-joins",
        "exact_quote": "A finite upper comparison implies the following assertions, simultaneously on each compact ordinary chart.*\n\n1.  *Every point has arbitrarily small surrounding primal circuits whose limiting costs tend to zero, uniformly over the compact set.*\n\n2.  *The functions $F_U$ are symmetric, satisfy the triangle inequality, and are locally continuous in their endpoints.         "exact_quote": "Consider a sequence of increasingly fine simultaneous annulus covers with fixed reference regularity cutoffs $a,A>0$.         "anchor": "stmt-comp-relation",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose that, on a coupled subsequence, $(V_n,\\delta_n)$ converges in Gromov–Hausdorff distance to a compact metric space $(Y,d_Y)$, and that $z_n(V_n)$ becomes dense in $\\widehat{\\mathbb C}$. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Finite rooted FK ensemble** ([source](#stmt-intro-finite-law)): Let $\mathcal F_n$ consist of pairs $(M,A)$, where $M$ is a connected planar multigraph with $n$ edges embedded in the oriented sphere and rooted at a distinguished oriented edge, and $A\subseteq E(M)$. Pairs are identified under orientation-preserving homeomorphisms preserving the root and $A$. Loops and multiple edges are allowed. Let $M^*$ be the dual map, and let $A^*$ consist of the dual edges crossing $E(M)\setminus A$. Write $k(A)$ and $k(A^*)$ for the numbers of connected components of the respective spanning subgraphs, including isolated vertices. Set $$\ell(M,A)=k(A)+k(A^*)-1 =2k(A)+\|A\|-\|V(M)\|, \qquad Z_n(q)=\sum_{(M,A)\in\mathcal F_n}q^{\ell(M,A)/2}.$$ We sample $(M_n,A_n)$ with probability $q^{\ell(M,A)/2}/Z_n(q)$. Its graph distance $d_n$ is shortest-path distance on $V(M_n)$ using all edges of $M_n$, each of length one.
- **Loop distance and ensemble matching** ([source](#stmt-intro-loop-topology)): Our curve distance and locally finite multiset topology follow Gwynne, Miller, and Qian (2021, sec. 2.2) [[GwynneMillerQianCLE](#ref-GwynneMillerQianCLE)], with loop orientation additionally forgotten. They retain the order within each loop and its multiplicity. For continuous loops $\alpha,\beta:\mathbb S^1\to\widehat{\mathbb C}$, let $$d_{\mathrm{loop}}(\alpha,\beta) =\inf_{\sigma}\sup_{t\in\mathbb S^1} \rho(\alpha(t),\beta(\sigma(t))),$$ where $\sigma$ ranges over circle homeomorphisms of either orientation. Identify loops at zero distance. A loop collection is locally finite in diameter if it has finitely many loops of diameter greater than $\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. An $\varepsilon$-matching of two such collections is a partial bijection covering every loop of diameter greater than $\varepsilon$ on either side, with matched loops at distance at most $\varepsilon$; every unmatched loop has diameter at most $\varepsilon$. Convergence means that such matchings exist with $\varepsilon\to0$. All collections in this paper retain nested loops.
- **Equilateral flag surface** ([source](#pm-h-11)): For each occurrence of an endpoint and a side of an original edge, take an equilateral triangle with labels $(v,e,f)$: original vertex, edge midpoint and face center.
- **Normalized flag area** ([source](#pm-h-11)): Give $X_n$ normalized Euclidean face area $m_n$, so each triangle has mass $1/(4n)$.
- **Full spatial distance graph** ([source](#intro:distance-graph)): Let $\Gamma_n$ be the images of the prescribed polygonal interfaces, with all nested loops retained, and let $$\label{intro:distance-graph} K_n(a)=\{(\phi_n(u),\phi_n(v),a d_n(u,v)):u,v\in V(M_n)\}.$$
- **Scalar contour-tree pseudometric** ([source](#pm-h-19)): For a continuous real function $c$ on a compact time interval, put $$\label{top:tree-pseudometric} d_c(s,t)=c(s)+c(t)-2\min_{[s\wedge t,s\vee t]}c.$$
- **Protected chart instruction** ([source](#stmt-ker-chart)): A chart instruction comprises these finite data. 1. Disjoint used time intervals, each strictly inside an extended block. Overlapping extended blocks are merged. A subinterval of a merged block retains its actual internal increments, without a new free starting height. 2. Finite unions of rational subintervals specifying ports, confining cells, supplier cells, and protected stars. Rational endpoints may be fractions of a block duration. A full star retains every incidence occurrence and its cyclic orientation at its primal and dual vertices. 3. For each coordinate $c$, a forest $F_c$ on the block indices, recording height differences at the *used* starts of blocks whose labelled scalar frontiers are compared. 4. Gluing bands, exact minima of specified retained subintervals, and a finite rational partition carrying types for externally unresolved flexible orders. Band endpoints have strict clearance, except at retained minimum heights, which are tested exactly on the lattice. Its realization uses the raw extended words, the forest differences, and these instructions. It retains the actual flag shapes and oriented gluings. A readout is a measurable function of this finite incidence record.
- **Forest lattice** ([source](#stmt-ker-lattice)): For $m$ used starts at even integer times put $$\Lambda_m=\{x=(x_i^1,x_i^2)_{i=1}^m\in\mathbb Z^{2m}: x_i^1+x_i^2\in2\mathbb Z\text{ for all }i\}.$$ Common height translation is immaterial. Let $P_F$ take the integer-linear differences specified by $F_1,F_2$, and set $\Lambda_F=P_F\Lambda_m$. If $x$ is the vector of raw integer start heights, the normalized forest parameter is $$\label{ker:forest-units} z=s_b n^{-1/2}P_Fx\in s_b n^{-1/2}\Lambda_F.$$ Sample it with probabilities proportional to a positive smooth density $\varpi_F(z)$. In raw diffusive coordinates $r=n^{-1/2}P_Fx$, the corresponding continuum density is $s_b^{d_F}\varpi_F(s_br)$, where $d_F=\operatorname{rank}P_F$. The fixed factor $s_b^{d_F}$ cancels in the lattice normalizing sum.
- **Unit flow** ([source](#conf:flow-bound)): A *unit flow* is a probability measure $\nu$ on rectifiable curves.
- **Extremal length** ([source](#conf:el-definition)): For a family $\mathcal C$ of curves on a Riemann surface, we use $$\mathop{\mathrm{EL}}(\mathcal C)= \sup_{\sigma} \frac{\bigl(\inf_{\gamma\in\mathcal C} \int_\gamma\sigma\,\mathrm ds\bigr)^2} {\int\sigma^2\,\mathrm dA}. \label{conf:el-definition}$$
- **Local passage comparisons and internal passage distance** ([source](#stmt-met-port-comparison)): Fix a joint limiting law of the field, its reference internal metrics, and the compatible ordered passage records. An *upper comparison with constant $C$* means the following simultaneous assertion. For every $D$-rectifiable path $P$ compactly contained in an open set $U$, every finite ordered subdivision of $P$, and every positive endpoint, tube, and cost tolerance, there is an attainable certificate which follows the subdivided path through those tolerances, with each marked subpassage costing at most $C$ times the corresponding $D$-length plus the assigned cost tolerance. An *upper constant* is a deterministic $C$ for which this holds almost surely in every ordinary chart. A *lower comparison with constant $c$* means that every finite-cost certificate, with limiting endpoints $x,y$, has cost at least $cD(x,y)$. It applies to every ordered subcertificate as well. A *lower constant* is a deterministic $c\geq0$ for which these assertions hold almost surely in every ordinary chart. For $x\ne y$ in $U$, let $F_U(x,y)$ be the infimum of the upper costs of certificates from $x$ to $y$ compactly confined in $U$, with the endpoint ports shrinking to $x,y$. Set $F_U(x,x)=0$.
- **Circuit quantile scale** ([source](#met:quantile)): Fix a quantile level $\tau<1$ sufficiently close to one, and define $$A_j=\inf\{t>0:\mathbb P[X_j\leq t]\geq\tau\}. \label{met:quantile}$$
- **Universal first-exit readout** ([source](#comp:escape-readout)): For nested spatial disks $U\Subset V\Subset W$, define $$\label{comp:escape-readout} E_n^{\mathrm o}(U,V)= \max_{\substack{u\in V_n\\x_n(u)\in U}} \delta_n\bigl(u,\{v\in V_n:x_n(v)\notin V\}\bigr).$$

| id | quantity | relation | value | regime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| q-coupling-weight | FK weight as a function of the quantum coupling | = | $2+2\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi\gamma^2}{2}\right)$ | The cluster weight is fixed throughout the convergence. |
| q-sle-parameter | SLE and CLE parameter | = | $\frac{16}{\gamma^2}$ | The parameter is determined by the fixed cluster weight. |
| q-inventory-parameter | Inventory flexible-order parameter | = | $\frac{\sqrt q}{2+\sqrt q}$ | The parameter fixes the rigid and flexible order probabilities. |
| q-flexible-order-probability | Probability of a flexible order | = | $\frac b2$ | The probability belongs to the fixed iid letter distribution. |
| q-interface-count | Number of FK interfaces encoded by a matched word | = | $1+N_{\mathsf F}$ | Flexible orders are counted in that finite word. |
| q-scalar-tree-perturbation | Uniform error in the scalar tree pseudometric | ≤ | $4\\|c_n-c\\|_\infty$ | The estimate is uniform over both contour times. |
| q-cone-survival-exponent | Joint-coordinate cone exponent | = | $\frac2{\gamma^2}$ | The exponent is determined by the fixed covariance. |
| q-record-image-dimension | Upper box dimension of the joint-record image | ≤ | $2(1-d_2)$ | The same bound applies to either coordinate projection. |
| q-quantum-cost-unit-change | Cost coordinate after an indexed change of quantum units | = | $v^{-p}O$ | This identity re-expresses an array; it does not equate differently indexed kernels. |
| q-annular-reciprocity | Product of annular through and winding extremal lengths | = | $1$ | The crossing and winding families belong to the same annulus. |
| q-reference-internal-holder | Confined reference connection distance | ≤ | $H\|x-y\|^\chi$ | Rectangle extensions retain bounded aspect ratio and strict collars. |
| q-chaining-upper-cost | Cost of following a reference path through surrounding circuits | ≤ | $\frac{L}{a}\operatorname{len}_D(P)+L\max_i w_i$ | The cover is fixed before the discrete approximation and then refined. |
| q-port-normalizer-ratio | Ratio of deterministic passage normalizers | ≤ | $K\left(\frac{n'}n\right)^s$ | The constants and the normalizer depend on the fixed model and test conventions. |
| q-port-normalizer-exponent | Admissible exponent in the polynomial normalizer-ratio bound | = | $p/2$ | Finite initial values may be changed. |
| q-final-metric-scalar | Product of the intrinsic-to-passage scale limit and the rigid passage multiplier | = | $1$ | Both factors are deterministic; equality follows from the common positive finite diameter law. |

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-finite-encoding** [claim](#stmt-enc-inventory-law) / [proof](#proof-stmt-enc-inventory-law): Inventory bijection, exact letter weights, and occurrence-wise tree/cotree sewing. -> The correct all-edge map, degree-area identity, interface count, and exact contour incidences.
- **step-continuum-reference** [claim](#stmt-enc-peanosphere) / [proof](#proof-stmt-enc-peanosphere): Contour invariance principles and continuum welding, with the explicit area-normalized sphere representation. -> A common curve-decorated quantum sphere and its finite-chain spatial identification rule.
- **step-projection-and-protection** [claim](#stmt-top-projection) / [proof](#proof-stmt-top-projection): Uniform scalar-tree continuity followed by spherical barycentric projection and complete-preimage compact protection. -> Small projected flags, faces, stars, and a finite time cover containing every tested occurrence.
- **step-local-lifts-and-skeleton** [claim](#stmt-top-skeleton-lift) / [proof](#proof-stmt-top-skeleton-lift): Finite scalar-chord chains, ordered path following, branch-set pruning, and facial correspondence. -> A primal subdivision following the reference skeleton with compatible faces.
- **step-topological-homeomorphisms** [claim](#stmt-top-homeomorphism) / [proof](#proof-stmt-top-homeomorphism): Jordan separation bounds face images, then disk extension and diagonal selection give measurable homeomorphisms. -> A common topological correspondence with vanishing error on finite spheres and protected bilateral tests.
- **step-robust-primal-separators** [claim](#stmt-top-separator-mesh) / [proof](#proof-stmt-top-separator-mesh): Strict transverse intersections and winding circuit extraction stitch supplied paths into separators. -> Connected primal separator meshes using only supplied walks and their costs.
- **step-local-exploration-genericity** [claim](#stmt-enc-chord-genericity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-enc-chord-genericity): Buffered imaginary-geometry locality, unique visits, cone estimates, and independent Gaussian translations exclude degeneracies. -> Finite local traversals and stable unique chronological supplier choices.
- **step-exact-protected-reconstruction** [claim](#stmt-ker-incidences) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ker-incidences): Recognize positive aligned scalar overlaps, separate omitted minima, and recompute retained lattice equalities exactly. -> A locally measurable finite incidence record containing every tested star and complete extended relative contour.
- **step-compact-observations** [claim](#stmt-ker-readouts) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ker-readouts): Compactify costs and retain closed finite path-record sets, numerical extremal lengths, and universal exit maxima jointly. -> Compatible finite-record limits with attainability and universal quantifiers preserved.
- **step-exact-word-resampling** [claim](#stmt-ker-word-ratio) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ker-word-ratio): Use parity-preserving ladder smoothing, complete reference packages, and an exact finite density cancellation before taking limits. -> Input-dependent limiting weights preserving the protected output kernel in bilateral and finite-bridge laws.
- **step-compatible-kernels** [claim](#stmt-ker-local-kernels) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ker-word-ratio-2): Disintegrate aggregate package limits and apply the input-density identity jointly across disjoint buffers. -> Common conditional kernels, conditional spatial products, density transfer, and joint indexed observations.
- **step-order-field-unit-transfer** [claim](#stmt-ker-field-transfer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ker-field-transfer): Finite-order augmentation, single-traversal localization, Gaussian restriction equivalence, and exact indexed unit identities. -> Compatible local laws across ordinary fields, fixed smooth shifts, coordinates, and quantum-unit conventions.
- **step-normalized-selected-transfers** [claim](#stmt-ker-sphere-density) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ker-sphere-density): Hold normalized inputs fixed in varying-label diagonals and compute actual-height sphere densities before selected Cameron–Martin changes. -> Actual finite-sphere output domination and positivity, together with valid domination after finite event selection.
- **step-aligned-annular-coverage** [claim](#stmt-ann-aligned-annuli) / [proof](#proof-stmt-ann-aligned-annuli): Conditional field transfer, all-order augmentation, Gaussian square budgets, and exterior-measurable label alignment. -> Simultaneous successful annuli at distinct radii around every point of each protected compact.
- **step-density-and-flow-compactness** [claim](#stmt-conf-flow-compactness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-conf-flow-compactness): Sum shell densities, charge all disjoint projected advances, and reparameterize flows using crossing counts. -> Nonconstant rectifiable limit flows with nonzero absolutely continuous average arclength.
- **step-conformal-nondegeneration** [claim](#stmt-conf-no-degeneration) / [proof](#proof-stmt-conf-no-degeneration): Deterministic rotation germs turn flow witnesses into transverse cheap crossings contradicting extremal-length reciprocity. -> Positive crossing quantiles and macroscopic extremal-length lower bounds.
- **step-canonical-conformal-coordinate** [claim](#stmt-conf-canonical) / [proof](#proof-stmt-conf-canonical): Apply all-center ring compactness, recover a local distortion tensor, eliminate anisotropy by rotations, and normalize actual area marks. -> The canonical coordinate, area convergence, vanishing maximum mesh, and diffuse conditional root sampling.
- **step-finite-chords-and-face-limits** [claim](#stmt-loop-convex) / [proof](#proof-stmt-loop-convex): Combine endpoint-pair convergence with exact finite surgery and convex-cell compactness while preserving cyclic order. -> Complete locally finite matchings of discrete interfaces with nonconstant limiting face curves.
- **step-complete-cle-identification** [claim](#stmt-loop-readout) / [proof](#proof-stmt-loop-readout): Use the alternating exploration dictionary, strict cone nesting, ordered prefix exhaustion, and winding witnesses for omitted strands. -> Every face curve is one complete nested CLE traversal and every CLE loop occurs once.
- **step-canonical-loop-law** [claim](#stmt-loop-canonical) / [proof](#proof-stmt-loop-canonical): Transport complete matchings by the common limiting coordinate and apply Möbius invariance conditional on fresh area marks. -> The canonical nested CLE collection with the fixed conditional law and common orientation sign.
- **step-reference-metric-and-chaining** [claim](#stmt-met-chain) / [proof](#proof-stmt-met-chain): Use internal reference regularity, geodesic anchors, ordered circuit intersections, and annular traversal lower tests. -> Ordered upper following and lower certificate bounds from simultaneous annulus covers.
- **step-finite-optimal-comparisons** [claim](#stmt-met-finite-upper) / [proof](#proof-stmt-met-finite-upper): Initial-growth first-failure arguments and preceding-scale quantile bounds yield finite attained optimal constants. -> A positive finite upper constant and a possibly vanishing lower constant, stable under retained tangent extraction.
- **step-extremal-saturated-tangent** [claim](#stmt-met-dense-anchors) / [proof](#proof-stmt-met-dense-anchors): Strict comparison improvement forces dense witness labels; a fixed-input diagonal and geodesic confluence give saturation at deterministic anchors. -> Under a strict constant gap, one tangent carries both exact anchor saturation and fixed-gap shortcuts.
- **step-shortcut-modification** [claim](#stmt-met-gate) / [proof](#proof-stmt-met-gate): Amplify auxiliary shortcuts in disjoint compartments and use a finite smooth wall-and-core recipe family. -> Every modified anchor geodesic admits a strict passage saving using the preserved shortcut.
- **step-weighted-rigidity** [claim](#stmt-met-rigidity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-met-rigidity): Dominate modification images before selection, compare weighted source and output counts, and recover continuous paths from positive lower cost. -> Coincident positive deterministic comparison constants and the internal passage metric identity.
- **step-all-scale-normalizers** [claim](#stmt-met-normalizers) / [proof](#proof-stmt-met-normalizers): Rigid quantile bounds, overlapping majority bands, and first-failure propagation control normalizers at all scales. -> Deterministic diverging normalizers with polynomial ratio control and rigid local comparisons on sphere patches.
- **step-location-relation-and-scale** [claim](#stmt-comp-scales) / [proof](#proof-stmt-comp-scales): Combine intrinsic compactness, all-vertex location relations, small root bypasses, and primal separators. -> A bounded deterministic comparison scale and vanishing intrinsic separators around every spatial point.

In any convergent joint extraction with additional reference or local observations, its metric component is the same graph <a href=\"#comp:target-graph\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"comp:target-graph\">[comp:target-graph]</a>. The Hausdorff metric for the second component is that induced by $\\rho(z,z')+\\rho(w,w')+|r-r'|$.",

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-joint-canonical-limit**: For the specified spherical FK ensemble and flag-triangle uniformization, area, full vertex-pair distance graphs, and nested interfaces converge jointly in the prescribed coordinate. The limiting loop law is independent of the embedded marked quantum surface.
- **invariant-ordered-loop-matching**: Loop convergence retains traversal order, multiplicity, and nesting. Matchings cover every macroscopic loop on either side, while loop orientation is forgotten.
- **invariant-protected-conditional-products**: Disjoint protected spatial buffers have product conditional output laws given the full continuum input. Observations within a common buffer remain part of one aggregate array.
- **invariant-all-vertex-completion**: The completed spatial distance graph records the reference metric at every spatial pair, including limits of atypical vertices and vertices approaching the exploration root.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-use-explicit-calibration**: Treat the convergence theorem as an executable calibration procedure for finite graph distances or as a finite-size error guarantee. -> Existence of a deterministic normalization does not supply a computable normalization or a convergence rate.
- **anti-use-deleting-primal-edges**: Compute distances using only occupied edges or only the auxiliary spanning tree. -> Deleting original primal edges changes the metric whose scaling limit is identified.
- **anti-use-trace-only-loop-validation**: Validate interface convergence solely by comparing the unions of loop traces. -> Trace agreement can lose traversal order, distinct loop occurrences, and nested components.
- **anti-use-topological-joining-as-cost-bound**: Use a spatially confined joining walk as a quantitative shortest-path estimate. -> Spatial confinement alone provides no control of the number of edges traversed.
- **anti-use-unconditional-buffer-independence**: Sample local observations independently without retaining their common continuum input. -> The product assertion is conditional on the continuum input, which can correlate the observations after integration.
- **anti-use-reidentifying-indexed-kernels**: Interpret a change of quantum units as equality of differently indexed passage kernels under an unchanged field. -> Re-expressing the same observation array changes its field, clock, boundary lengths, and cost units together.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The engineering target is joint convergence to a continuum random surface and its complete nested loop ensemble, rather than a finite constructive decision problem. The main theorem asserts existence of a deterministic normalization, and the source explicitly states: “All assertions are for a fixed $q$; the proof gives no endpoint assertion, convergence rate or explicit formula for $a_n$.” Finite checks of incidence identities or sampled contours would not decide this joint convergence theorem or certify its conditional independence and all-vertex completion.

## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-fixed-interior-parameter** (hypothesis): Convergence is asserted for a fixed cluster weight in the specified open range. Endpoint limits and changing-parameter limits require separate results. Blocked use: ['Applying the canonical limit at an endpoint of the parameter range.', 'Letting the cluster weight vary with map size without an additional theorem.']
- **limit-specific-spherical-ensemble** (hypothesis): The input is the stated rooted spherical planar multigraph ensemble with its FK decoration weights. Planarity alone does not establish the required probability law. Blocked use: ['Applying the random limit to an arbitrary planar graph sequence.', 'Transferring the result to deterministic triangulations or general directed graphs.']
- **limit-all-original-edges** (hypothesis): The graph metric uses all original primal edges, independently of occupation status and auxiliary tree membership. Blocked use: ['Replacing the graph metric by occupied-subgraph distance.', 'Using auxiliary spanning-tree distance as the metric in the main theorem.']
- **limit-incidence-occurrences** (edge_case): Loops and bridges require distinct incidence occurrences even when their labels coincide. Blocked use: ['Deduplicating flags or interface ports by vertex, edge, or face labels alone.']
- **limit-prescribed-uniformization-marks** (hypothesis): The canonical coordinate uses fresh independent flag-area samples. Exploration marks cannot replace those samples. Blocked use: ['Normalizing the conformal embedding with the exploration root or previously selected traversal marks.']
- **limit-no-effective-normalization** (nonconstructive): The metric normalization is established by existence and distributional identification; an explicit formula and convergence rate are ABSENT. Blocked use: ['Claiming a computable finite-size metric calibration from the main theorem.', 'Assigning a numerical approximation tolerance from the asymptotic convergence alone.']
- **limit-topological-walks-have-no-cost-bound** (formal_scope): Local joining controls spatial confinement but gives no bound on graph-walk length. Blocked use: ['Inferring a shortest-path approximation or execution budget from topological local joining.']
- **limit-complete-local-protection** (hypothesis): Protected reconstruction retains every needed time preimage and full incidence star, with strict margins and exact retained lattice tests. Blocked use: ['Reconstructing a protected observation from a selected visit while omitting other incidences.', 'Inferring exact lattice equalities solely from uniform contour convergence.']
- **limit-finite-records-not-continuous-paths** (formal_scope): Attainability of finite path records does not alone produce a continuous limiting path; an additional continuity modulus is required. Blocked use: ['Promoting a limiting spatial range or finite record directly to a parameterized continuous path.']
- **limit-conditional-buffer-products** (formal_scope): Product output laws are conditional on the full continuum input and concern disjoint closed spatial buffers. Constituent blocks of one buffer are aggregated. Blocked use: ['Assuming unconditional independence of local observations.', 'Sampling constituent time-block outputs independently within one spatial buffer.']
- **limit-input-density-preconditions** (hypothesis): Kernel preservation requires the exact resampling identity, bounded convergent weights on the chart, and a positive limiting normalizer. Blocked use: ['Preserving a conditional output kernel under an arbitrary output-dependent reweighting.', 'Treating a missing or vanishing normalizer as an admissible density change.']
- **limit-indexed-unit-reexpression** (formal_scope): Changing quantum units re-expresses the same indexed array and transforms its field, clock, boundary lengths, and costs together. Blocked use: ['Identifying differently indexed kernels under an unchanged field.', 'Applying a cost scaling rule without changing its associated input units.']
- **limit-varying-label-diagonal** (hypothesis): The varying-label diagonal holds with a fixed normalized reference input law and diverging effective microscopic units; it does not cover arbitrary varying field densities. Blocked use: ['Extracting a varying-label limit while retaining a bounded effective microscopic scale.', 'Replacing the common normalized input law by unrestricted varying densities.']
- **limit-sphere-actual-heights-and-mass** (hypothesis): Joint sphere transfer retains actual additive heights and applies on separated patches avoiding the marks; positivity is restricted by the patch mass event. Blocked use: ['Using equivalence modulo constants as a joint law for actual heights.', 'Asserting unrestricted equivalence of normalized sphere and ordinary field restrictions.']
- **limit-selection-before-domination** (hypothesis): The pinned Gaussian law and finite deterministic shift menu are fixed before auxiliary draws and event selection, and domination uses a likelihood cutoff. Blocked use: ['Repinning the realized field after selecting a shortcut.', 'Assuming independence survives selection of a rare hit.', 'Dropping the likelihood cutoff from selected-law domination.']
- **limit-annular-test-order-of-limits** (formal_scope): A finite annular configuration and its strict margins are fixed before taking the discrete threshold. Subsequent refinement is diagonal and supplies no discrete convergence rate. Blocked use: ['Choosing a shrinking test radius depending on the discrete index without an additional uniform estimate.']
- **limit-probability-one-versus-tail-transfer** (formal_scope): A fixed absolutely continuous field-law change preserves the eventual annular conclusion but need not preserve the numerical summable probability bound. Blocked use: ['Transferring the ordinary Gaussian exponential failure bound unchanged to every absolutely continuous field law.']
- **limit-free-ports-before-endpoint-completion** (formal_scope): Local upper passage comparison permits free choices inside endpoint ports and does not yet bound access to a prescribed lattice vertex. Blocked use: ['Claiming all-vertex metric convergence from local port rigidity alone.', 'Omitting intrinsic completion near atypical vertices or the exploration root.']
- **limit-intrinsic-companion-input** (hypothesis): All-vertex completion and deterministic scale identification use the companion intrinsic convergence. The stronger measured conclusion and separate spanning-tree result are not inputs to this argument. Blocked use: ['Presenting the all-vertex metric conclusion as following from contour convergence or conformal comparison alone.', 'Silently replacing the stated intrinsic input by a different map law or metric normalization.']
- **limit-ordered-nested-loop-topology** (formal_scope): Loop convergence retains traversal order, multiplicity, and nesting while forgetting orientation. Trace-set convergence alone is weaker. Blocked use: ['Validating convergence by the union of interface traces alone.', 'Discarding repeated or nested loops before constructing matchings.']
- **limit-common-orientation-and-law** (hypothesis): Removal of the common adaptive reflection is a joint-law argument requiring invariance of both marginal laws. It does not justify independent orientation choices for different components. Blocked use: ['Reflecting area, metric, and loop components separately.', 'Removing an adaptive sign using symmetry of only one marginal law.']
- **limit-finite-checks-do-not-certify-continuum-limit** (nonconstructive): Finite incidence and reduction constructions can be checked separately, but finite enumeration does not decide the joint continuum convergence or the existence of its normalization. Blocked use: ['Reporting finite combinatorial checks as certification of the full canonical scaling theorem.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


For every fixed $`0\lt q\lt 4`$, we prove joint convergence of spherical Fortuin–Kasteleyn planar maps in their flag-triangle uniformization to the corresponding unit-area Liouville quantum gravity sphere decorated by an independent conformal loop ensemble. The convergence includes the area measure, deterministically rescaled graph distances between all vertex pairs, and the full nested interface collection, with interfaces converging uniformly up to reparameterization.

<a id="intro:section"></a>
### Introduction

Random planar maps give discrete models of random surfaces. A central problem is to identify their scaling limits in prescribed conformal coordinates, together with area, intrinsic distance and a statistical mechanical decoration. The continuum area measure of Liouville quantum gravity (LQG) is a Gaussian multiplicative chaos measure. Its construction belongs to Kahane’s theory (Kahane 1985) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[KahaneChaos1985](#ref-KahaneChaos1985)]; Duplantier and Sheffield developed the circle-average construction for LQG and proved the probabilistic KPZ relation (Duplantier and Sheffield 2011) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[DuplantierSheffieldKPZ2011](#ref-DuplantierSheffieldKPZ2011)]. For maps decorated by the critical Fortuin–Kasteleyn (FK) random-cluster model (Fortuin and Kasteleyn 1972) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[FortuinKasteleyn1972](#ref-FortuinKasteleyn1972)], the interfaces are predicted to converge to a conformal loop ensemble (CLE), independent of the LQG surface in its conformal coordinate.

The discrete route to this prediction begins with tree-decorated maps. Mullin’s correspondence and Bernardi’s bijective developments encode such maps through pairs of tree contours (Mullin 1967; Bernardi 2007) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[Mullin1967](#ref-Mullin1967), [Bernardi2007](#ref-Bernardi2007)]. Sheffield’s inventory bijection combines this description with Bernardi’s subgraph-to-tree construction (Bernardi 2008; Sheffield 2015) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[Bernardi2008Subgraphs](#ref-Bernardi2008Subgraphs), [SheffieldInventory](#ref-SheffieldInventory)]. It encodes an FK-decorated map by a word whose two resolved contours have a correlated Brownian scaling limit. Duplantier–Miller–Sheffield identify the continuum mating with an LQG surface carrying an independent space-filling Schramm–Loewner evolution (SLE); Miller–Sheffield give the finite-area sphere version (Duplantier, Miller, and Sheffield 2021; Miller and Sheffield 2019) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[DMSMating](#ref-DMSMating), [MillerSheffieldSphere](#ref-MillerSheffieldSphere)]. Gwynne, Mao and Sun, and Gwynne and Sun, strengthen the discrete convergence to retain cone times and encoded FK-loop information, including quantum areas and boundary lengths. Their finite-volume result applies to words conditioned to reduce to the empty word (Gwynne, Mao, and Sun 2019; Gwynne and Sun 2017, 2015) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[GwynneMaoSunFKI](#ref-GwynneMaoSunFKI), [GwynneSunFKII](#ref-GwynneSunFKII), [GwynneSunFKIII](#ref-GwynneSunFKIII)].

These results identify the limit through its encoding. Convergence in a prescribed discrete conformal embedding requires a further comparison with the embedded geometry. An intrinsic metric-space limit alone likewise does not specify where the discrete vertices lie in that coordinate (Miller and Sheffield 2019; Gwynne, Holden, and Sun 2023) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[MillerSheffieldSphere](#ref-MillerSheffieldSphere), [GHS-survey](#ref-GHS-survey)]. Gwynne, Miller and Sheffield proved convergence of the Tutte embedding of mated-CRT maps, jointly with quantum area, the space-filling curve and embedded random walk (Gwynne, Miller, and Sheffield 2021, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[GwynneMillerSheffieldTutte](#ref-GwynneMillerSheffieldTutte)]. Holden and Sun proved joint metric and measure convergence under the Cardy embedding for uniform triangulations of polygons at $\gamma=\sqrt{8/3}$, together with convergence of independent percolation decorations (Holden and Sun 2023, Theorems 1.3 and 1.6) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[HS-Cardy](#ref-HS-Cardy)]. Holden and Yu proved large-scale comparison results for circle packing and Riemann uniformization of infinite planar maps in ergodic scale-free environments under geometric moment and connectivity hypotheses (Holden and Yu 2026, Theorems 1.6–1.9) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[HoldenYuUniformization](#ref-HoldenYuUniformization)]. These results concern different map laws or embedding inputs from the finite spherical FK model studied here. A general conformal-embedding universality conjecture is recorded as Conjecture 3.5 of Holden and Sun (2025) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[HS-survey](#ref-HS-survey)].

Here we prove the joint statement for the flag-triangle uniformization of critical spherical FK maps, for every fixed $0<q<4$. This establishes the canonical conformal, area, intrinsic-metric and interface limit for this specified model and embedding within the broader universality prediction. Here “subcritical” refers to the LQG range $\gamma<2$, equivalently $q<4$; the FK model itself is at its self-dual critical point. The intrinsic step uses the distinct metric companion (OpenAI 2026, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[Intrinsic-input](#ref-Intrinsic-input)]; we restate precisely its required unmarked Gromov–Hausdorff consequence in <a href="#intro:intrinsic-input" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:intrinsic-input">2</a>. The new comparison identifies all these objects in the same canonical coordinate, including atypical vertices and the order along every macroscopic loop.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### The result

<a id="intro:parameters"></a>
<a id="intro:distance-graph"></a>
Fix $q\in(0,4)$. Let $\gamma\in(\sqrt2,2)$ and $\kappa\in(4,8)$ be determined by $$\label{intro:parameters}
 q=2+2\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi\gamma^2}{2}\right),
 \qquad \kappa=\frac{16}{\gamma^2}.$$ The finite law and all topologies are specified in <a href="#intro:model-section" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:model-section">2</a>. In brief, a rooted $n$-edge decorated map $(M_n,A_n)$ has weight $q^{\ell(M_n,A_n)/2}$, where $\ell$ counts FK interfaces. Its $4n$ equilateral flag triangles form a conformal sphere $X_n$ with normalized face area $m_n$. Three independent $m_n$ points determine the orientation-preserving uniformization $\phi_n:X_n\to\widehat{\mathbb C}$ by their images $0,1,\infty$. Distances $d_n$ use every original primal edge. Let $\Gamma_n$ be the images of the prescribed polygonal interfaces, with all nested loops retained, and let $$\label{intro:distance-graph}
 K_n(a)=\{(\phi_n(u),\phi_n(v),a d_n(u,v)):u,v\in V(M_n)\}.$$

On the continuum side, take the ordinary unit-area $\gamma$-LQG sphere, forget its original marks, and normalize its conformal embedding using three independent quantum-area points at $0,1,\infty$. Denote the resulting area measure and intrinsic metric by $\mu_h$ and $D_h$. Fix the deterministic normalization of $D_h$ throughout. Conditional on this embedded surface, let $\Gamma$ have the Möbius-invariant whole-plane nested $\mathrm{CLE}_{\kappa}$ law on $\widehat{\mathbb C}$.

<a id="stmt-intro-main"></a>
<div id="intro:main" class="theorem">

<a id="intro:joint-convergence"></a>
<a id="intro:mesh-conclusion"></a>
**Theorem 1** (Joint canonical limit). *There is a deterministic sequence $a_n=a_n(q)>0$ with $a_n\to0$ such that, through all positive integers, $$\label{intro:joint-convergence}
 \big((\phi_n)_*m_n,K_n(a_n),\Gamma_n\big)
 \ \Longrightarrow\
 \big(\mu_h,\{(z,w,D_h(z,w)):z,w\in\widehat{\mathbb C}\},\Gamma\big).$$ The three topologies are weak convergence of probability measures, Hausdorff convergence of the full distance graphs, and uniform reparameterization matching of loop collections as defined in <a href="#intro:loop-topology" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:loop-topology">5</a>. Moreover, $$\label{intro:mesh-conclusion}
 \max_{T\text{ a flag triangle of }X_n}
       \mathop{\mathrm{diam}}_{\rho}\phi_n(T)\ \longrightarrow\ 0
 \qquad\text{in probability},$$ where $\rho$ is spherical distance. The conditional law of $\Gamma$ is independent of the embedded marked quantum surface.*

</div>

On a coupling with the asserted convergence, the distance-graph conclusion controls every pair of vertices whose embedded positions converge, including vertices with atypical degrees or near the exploration root. The loop topology retains the order along each curve and its multiplicity, as well as its trace. These conclusions are simultaneous in the prescribed coordinate. All assertions are for a fixed $q$; the proof gives no endpoint assertion, convergence rate or explicit formula for $a_n$.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
#### The intrinsic input

<a id="stmt-intro-intrinsic-input"></a>
<div id="intro:intrinsic-input" class="theorem">

**Theorem 2** (Intrinsic spherical scaling; companion consequence). *For the finite law of <a href="#intro:finite-law" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:finite-law">3</a> and $\gamma$ in <a href="#intro:parameters" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="intro:parameters">[intro:parameters]</a>, there is a deterministic sequence $a_n>0$ with $a_n\to0$ such that $$(V(M_n),a_n d_n)\ \Longrightarrow\ (S,D_h)$$ in the Gromov–Hausdorff topology on compact metric spaces up to isometry, through all positive integers. The limit is the ordinary unit-area $\gamma$-LQG sphere of Duplantier, Miller, and Sheffield (2021, Definition 4.21(ii)) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[DMSMating](#ref-DMSMating)], disintegrated at total quantum area one, with its marked points forgotten and with the fixed intrinsic metric normalization. The root and FK decoration are forgotten in this convergence.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-intro-intrinsic-input"><summary>Proof of stmt-intro-intrinsic-input</summary>

*Proof.* Apply the fixed-$q$ FK clause of OpenAI (2026, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[Intrinsic-input](#ref-Intrinsic-input)] and forget the degree measure from its Gromov–Hausdorff–Prokhorov conclusion. The finite law, all-edge distance, ordinary unit-area sphere law and fixed metric normalization are exactly those above. ◻

</details>

The companion *Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps*, by OpenAI, September 24, 2026, proves the intrinsic result. We use only the displayed GH consequence; its stronger measured conclusion and its separate spanning-tree clause are not needed here. We take the same deterministic $a_n(q)$ throughout. In the companion the vertex measure is $\deg(v)/(2n)$, with loops counted twice. Each vertex belongs to $2\deg(v)$ of the $4n$ flag occurrences, so projection of uniform flag area to its vertex has exactly that degree distribution. The Brownian encoding uses $2n$ letters and an area clock of duration one; neither this clock normalization nor the flag geometry changes the all-edge metric. The role of <a href="#intro:intrinsic-input" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:intrinsic-input">2</a> is to complete locally identified passage metrics at every vertex and to fix the deterministic scale.

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
#### Proof strategy

We first place the discrete and continuum objects on one topological sphere. The contour limit and its continuum sewing are recalled in <a href="#enc:section" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="enc:section">3</a>. In <a href="#top:section" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="top:section">4</a> they give homeomorphisms $H_n$ from the complete flag surface to the reference LQG sphere, with every flag image small. These homeomorphisms preserve separation and intersections but do not yet compare conformal moduli or lengths.

Here is the local information needed for those comparisons. Take a compact disk inside a larger open region of the reference sphere. Retain every exploration-time visit to the disk, together with a buffer around those visits and every incidence at their primal and dual vertices. There are finitely many retained time blocks. Their raw words, relative contour heights and exact minimum tests determine the corresponding part of the discrete flag surface. One can then read, for example, the minimum graph cost between two small endpoint sets, or the extremal length of curves joining two sides of a quadrilateral. [local:section](#local:section) constructs these finite records; retaining all visits is what makes their conclusions apply to every local path and vertex.

The continuum contours need not determine a subsequential discrete readout. [ker:section](#ker:section) instead identifies its conditional law: given the full continuum surface and exploration, the readout depends only on the retained local input, and disjoint protected regions have product conditional laws. An exact word-resampling identity shows that changes from the bilateral word to the finite conditioned word alter only the density of the continuum input. The same kernels then transfer to ordinary Gaussian fields and to the sphere at its actual area-normalized height. [ann:section](#ann:section) turns local events with high probability into successful annuli at many radii around every point. This supplies the common probabilistic input for the conformal and metric comparisons.

<a id="pm-h-6"></a>
###### Conformal coordinate and area.

[conf:section](#conf:section) rules out degeneration of flag-surface extremal length. A hypothetically small crossing modulus gives a probability flow of paths with low traffic energy. Annular lower bounds force its projected limit to consist of nonconstant rectifiable curves whose average arclength is absolutely continuous with respect to planar area. Locality and rotation covariance then give cheap crossings in two transverse directions at the same point, contradicting quadrilateral reciprocity. The resulting annular bounds give a quasiconformal limit of $\phi_n\circ H_n^{-1}$. Its infinitesimal conformal structure is read from local moduli; triviality of the field germ and rotation covariance make it round. Three area marks fix the resulting conformal map, and the area and maximum-mesh conclusions follow in that coordinate. The analytic framework comes from Ahlfors–Beurling extremal length (Ahlfors and Beurling 1952) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[AhlforsBeurling1952ConformalInvariants](#ref-AhlforsBeurling1952ConformalInvariants)] and the ring estimates of Ivrii–Marković (Ivrii and Marković 2019) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[IvriiMarkovic2019](#ref-IvriiMarkovic2019)]. The elimination of deterministic anisotropy by rotation covariance has a related use in Holden and Yu (2026, sec. 4.4) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[HoldenYuUniformization](#ref-HoldenYuUniformization)], where determinism comes from averaged Dirichlet energies.

<a id="pm-h-7"></a>
###### Ordered nested interfaces.

[loop:section](#loop:section) identifies the loops independently of the metric comparison. Flexible-order matches form a noncrossing chord system on the exploration-time circle. Its faces encode the finite FK loops, including their cyclic traversal order. Chord convergence first gives ordered limits of these face contours. The alternating CLE exploration identifies their initial portions; winding tests on both sides exclude an omitted moving portion. This matches every macroscopic loop, with multiplicity, and retains the full nested collection. The exploration convention follows Sheffield (2009; Miller and Sheffield 2017) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[SheffieldExplorationTrees](#ref-SheffieldExplorationTrees), [MillerSheffieldIGIV](#ref-MillerSheffieldIGIV)] and the nested construction described in Aru et al. (2022, sec. 2.1.6) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[AruHoldenPowellSunCritical](#ref-AruHoldenPowellSunCritical)].

<a id="pm-h-8"></a>
###### Local passages and all-vertex distances.

In <a href="#met:section" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="met:section">10</a>, graph passages between small endpoint sets first acquire upper and lower comparisons with the reference LQG metric. Repeated annular opportunities and local finite-energy field changes bring a reference geodesic near a shortcut. A weighted change-of-measure argument forces the optimal comparison constants to agree. This adapts the optimal-constant method of Gwynne and Miller (Gwynne and Miller 2021b, sec. 1.5 and Sections 3–6) <a id="pm-cite-21"></a>[[GwynneMillerMetric](#ref-GwynneMillerMetric)] to the local passage kernels. The changed laws are compared before a shortcut or a geodesic hit is selected, so restriction to a rare selected event preserves the required domination.

These passages have freely chosen endpoints in small sets; reaching a prescribed lattice vertex is a separate problem. [comp:section](#comp:section) uses <a href="#intro:intrinsic-input" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:intrinsic-input">2</a> at this point. Small surrounding circuits and the sphere topology of the GH limit exclude nontrivial spatial fibers. A possible collapse of all local passage costs would concentrate the remaining metric at one spatial point; the joint local laws exclude it by placing two separated positive escape-cost tests in the same sphere. The resulting all-vertex metric is a deterministic multiple of $D_h$, and the intrinsic diameter law fixes that multiple. All field-law arguments use the original oriented reference coordinate; only then are their geometric conclusions transported to the canonical coordinate. [joint:section](#joint:section) assembles the three branches, including their common marks and possible common reflection. Figure <a href="#intro:roadmap-figure" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:roadmap-figure">1</a> records these dependencies.

<figure id="intro:roadmap-figure">

<figcaption>The conformal, loop and metric arguments share the contour correspondence. The intrinsic GH input enters only the all-vertex completion of the metric.</figcaption>
</figure>
